# CI and releases

Loaded when working under `.github/`. What every change runs before its pull request, and which statuses matter for a merge, are in the root `AGENTS.md` (CI).

## CI (GitHub Actions, public repository)

- The repository is public: GitHub-hosted runners, macOS included, cost nothing and have no monthly quota, so what CI spares is waiting time. Pull requests run on Linux (`ubuntu-24.04`, NFR-7); a push to `main` and the nightly run (03:17 UTC) run `check` on macOS (`macos-latest`), which shows what only macOS shows within one merge; `openspec` and `codex` run on Linux always.
- Which jobs have work is decided by `tools/ci/changed-paths.sh` (plain shell, tested in `tools/ci/changed-paths.test.ts`) on a checkout of depth 2: `check` has nothing to do for a pull request whose diff holds only `docs/` (except the three files tests and the view build read: `DESIGN.md`, the PRD addendum and the spine), `openspec/`, `drafts/` or Markdown outside the packages, `skills/` and `hooks/` (not `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `CHANGELOG.md` at the root), and `codex` has nothing to do unless an instruction file (`AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, at the root or nested), `.claude/`, `.mcp.json` or `setup.sh` changed (always on the nightly run). The e2e jobs read the same `code` output. A job with nothing to do still runs and ends after one step, so every status exists for every change under the same name.
- Triggers: `openspec`, `check` and `codex` run automatically, on every pull request, on every push to `main` and nightly. A newer push to a pull request cancels its running workflow; a push to `main`, the nightly run and a dispatch are never cancelled (their concurrency group is the commit). `e2e.yml` runs the browser and conformance suites on a cadence: on every pull request, on Linux, the browser smoke set in Chromium and conformance on Bun; every night (02:23 UTC), on Linux, every browser file in each engine the manifest gives it in four shards per engine, the perf pass and conformance on Node 24 and 26; every Saturday (04:23 UTC) and before every release, on macOS, the nightly's set with conformance on Bun, Node 24 and 26; `workflow_dispatch` takes the `cadence`. Run `bun run test:e2e:smoke` before every pull request that touches the view, the server or the conformance suite, and `bun run test:e2e` before one that changes the harness, the runner or a widget's rendering. A new browser file is listed in the suite manifest (`packages/view/test/browser/harness/suites.ts`) or a test fails. On a hosted runner the perf pass scales every timed bound and its waits by a factor per runner OS, 2 on Linux and 3 on macOS, from `ASKBOARD_PERF_RUNNER` (`${{ runner.os }}`, set only on `browser.yml`'s test step; unset is 1, any other value fails the run), through `PERF_FACTOR` and `perfScaled` in `packages/view/test/browser/harness/perf.ts`. The macOS job turns keyboard navigation on before any browser starts (`defaults write -g AppleKeyboardUIMode -int 2`, the step "Keyboard navigation on (macOS)"), since Cocoa WebKit tabs to buttons only with it on; a Mac with it off fails the keyboard cases on WebKit ("ten presses of Tab never reached Answer"): set it in System Settings > Keyboard (Keyboard navigation). Actions are pinned by commit SHA with the version as a comment; Dependabot bumps them and the Bun dependencies weekly, minor and patch bumps grouped in one pull request per ecosystem (a major gets its own), except `@types/bun`, which is bumped by hand together with the Bun pin in `packageManager` (a workspace test fails if they differ).
- Branch rulesets and code scanning are available on a public repository. A failing check blocks a merge only through a ruleset on `main` that requires it, a setting of the repository and not of git: the statuses are `openspec / OpenSpec validate`, `check / Type check, lint, tests, import and licence checks` and `codex / Codex files from the sources`. Until a ruleset requires them, check CI before merging. The e2e statuses are not required checks (the PO's answer, 2026-11-14), so a red e2e job blocks no merge.

## Releases

- A release is the manual workflow `.github/workflows/release.yml`, dispatched on `main`: preflight (versions agree, tag `v<version>` free, a `## <version>` section in `CHANGELOG.md`, Claude Code's `stable` at or above `CLAUDE_CODE_MINIMUM`), the check, the build, the assembly, the smoke on macOS and on Linux, the browser and conformance suites on macOS (`e2e-macos`, the weekly cadence, in Chromium and WebKit until #174 and #145 close, with Firefox's smoke set on Linux in `e2e-firefox-smoke`), then `publish` (the only job with write access) commits the tree to `release`, tags it and creates the GitHub release. To release: `bun tools/release/version.ts <x.y.z>`, a CHANGELOG section naming only what has merged, `ROADMAP.md` brought up to the release, merge, dispatch.

```sh
bun tools/release/version.ts <x.y.z>                 # one version in every manifest and bun.lock (a test fails when they differ)
bun tools/release/assemble.ts --out <empty dir>      # after bun run build: the release tree and its marketplace file
node tools/release/smoke.ts <tree> --tools <file>    # the tree on plain Node (tool names from tools/release/tool-names.ts)
bun tools/release/package.ts --tree <tree> --out <dir> # notes.md, askboard-<version>.mjs and .zip, SHA256SUMS
```
